### voxy.pronounce.align_words(text, words)

`{index of a word of text: index of the ASR word heard for it}`.

Words are matched by aligning the two sequences (`difflib`), so a word ASR missed,
merged or added elsewhere does not shift the others; a text word with no exact
counterpart is left out.

```pycon
>>> align_words("Il est là", [{"text": " Il"}, {"text": " et"}, {"text": " est"}, {"text": " là."}])
{0: 0, 1: 2, 2: 3}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]

### voxy.pronounce.audit(text, audio, \*, readings=None, language='fr', expected=None, detectors=(), emitter=None, words_of=<function \_transcribed_words>, scoring='phrase', phonemize=None, context=1, filler_penalty=1.0, padding=0.08, margin=None)

Which reading did each heteronym of `text` get in the finished `audio`?

ASR (WER) checks cannot answer this: Whisper writes “est” whether the model said
/ɛ/ or /ɛst/. This flags the words of `text` that have several readings
([`voxy.speechtext.flag_risks()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.flag_risks)), finds each in the audio (ASR word times; the
n-th time the text has a word is the n-th time ASR heard it) and scores its
readings with the phoneme recogniser.

* **Parameters:**
  * **text** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – What the model was given (the speech text, not the display text).
  * **audio** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike)) – The render.
  * **readings** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `{word: {reading name: IPA}}`; default [`heteronym_readings()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.heteronym_readings)
    for `language`.
  * **expected** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – The reading each word should have: `{word: reading}`, or
    `risk -> reading` to decide per occurrence (`risk.line`, `risk.word`).
    Otherwise what a `detectors` entry found for that word on that line
    (e.g. [`voxy.speechtext.pos_detector()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.pos_detector)), else None (just report).
  * **detectors** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)]]) – `text -> risks` proposers of expected readings.
  * **emitter** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)], [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – The phoneme recogniser; default [`phoneme_emitter()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.phoneme_emitter).
  * **words_of** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)]]) – `audio -> timed words`; default ASR (`voxy.refprep.transcribe`).
  * **scoring** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – How a reading is scored in the audio. `"phrase"` (default): the
    `context` words on each side are written out with `phonemize` and each
    reading is scored as the whole phrase ([`phrase_readings()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.phrase_readings)); the
    neighbours are the same in every candidate, so only the word decides.
    `"spot"`: the reading is spotted in that window, the rest left to filler
    ([`spot_readings()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.spot_readings); no phonemizer, but a neighbour’s /s/ or /t/ can be
    credited to the longer reading). `"crop"`: the word alone, cut at its ASR
    times (`padding` each side), scored by [`score_readings()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.score_readings); ASR word
    times are often too loose for this.
  * **phonemize** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – For `"phrase"`; default [`espeak_phonemizer()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.espeak_phonemizer).
  * **context** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Words kept on each side of the flagged one.
  * **margin** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – See [`Verdict.decided`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Verdict.decided); default [`DFLT_CONTEXT_MARGIN`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.DFLT_CONTEXT_MARGIN),
    [`DFLT_SPOT_MARGIN`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.DFLT_SPOT_MARGIN) or [`DFLT_MARGIN`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.DFLT_MARGIN) by `scoring`.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Finding`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Finding)]

Returns the findings in text order; `[f for f in findings if f.ok is False]` are
the words decidedly misread (re-render those), `f.ok is None` ones were not
decided or not found.

### voxy.pronounce.best_reading(log_probs, vocab, readings, , blank=None)

The name of the reading `log_probs` support best.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### voxy.pronounce.checks_by_line(risks, , readings, expected=None)

[`checks_from_risks()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.checks_from_risks), grouped by the line each risk is on.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]]]

### voxy.pronounce.checks_from_risks(risks, , readings, expected=None)

`verify_words` checks for the flagged words that have known IPA readings.

`readings` maps a word (case-insensitively) to `{name: IPA}`, e.g. from a
Lexique-derived heteronym list the caller supplies; `expected` names the
reading each word should have, and otherwise the risks’ own `expected` (what a
detector such as `voxy.speechtext.pos_detector` found) is used. Words with no
entry are skipped. Each word is checked once: `verify_words` finds every place
it is spoken, so a word whose risks name *different* readings gets none here
(group the risks by line with [`checks_by_line()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.checks_by_line) to check each one).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]]

### voxy.pronounce.ctc_log_likelihood(log_probs, target, , blank=0)

`log P(target | log_probs)` under CTC (the forward algorithm, in log space).

`log_probs` is `frames x vocab` (log-softmax). `-inf` when the target cannot
be aligned (more symbols than frames allow).

```pycon
>>> lp = log_probs_from_path([1, 2], vocab_size=3)
>>> ctc_log_likelihood(lp, [1, 2]) > ctc_log_likelihood(lp, [2, 1])
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### voxy.pronounce.espeak_phonemizer(, model='facebook/wav2vec2-lv-60-espeak-cv-ft', threads=None, rootdir=None)

The default [`Phonemizer`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Phonemizer): espeak-ng (bundled by `espeakng-loader`), run in
the recogniser’s env, so its IPA is the recogniser’s own alphabet.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

### voxy.pronounce.failing(verdicts)

The verdicts whose word was decidedly read the wrong way (`ok is False`).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Verdict`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Verdict)]

### voxy.pronounce.heteronym_readings(language='fr')

voxy’s own heteronym table for `language`: `{word: {reading name: IPA}}`.

A short, hand-made list (French: *est*, *fils*, *plus*, *tous*, the  *-ent* verbs…);
merge a fuller one (e.g. derived from Lexique) read with [`load_readings()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.load_readings).

```pycon
>>> heteronym_readings("fr")["est"]["noun"]
'ɛst'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

### voxy.pronounce.known_symbols(ipa, vocab)

The symbols of `ipa` the recogniser knows, longest first; stress marks, spaces
and anything else it never emits are dropped.

```pycon
>>> known_symbols("ˈtʁist ɛ", ["<pad>", "t", "ʁ", "i", "s", "ɛ"])
['t', 'ʁ', 'i', 's', 't', 'ɛ']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### voxy.pronounce.load_readings(path)

Heteronym readings `{word: {reading name: IPA}}` from a caller’s file.

A `.json` file holds that mapping; any other file is tab-separated
`word<TAB>reading name<TAB>IPA`, one reading per line (`#` lines and blank
lines skipped), e.g. a list derived from Lexique, which voxy does not ship.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

### voxy.pronounce.log_probs_from_path(path, , vocab_size, confidence=0.9)

Log-probabilities of a recogniser that hears `path` (one id per frame).

A test and doctest helper: each frame gives `confidence` to its id and shares
the rest evenly.

```pycon
>>> log_probs_from_path([0], vocab_size=2).round(2).tolist()
[[-0.11, -2.3]]
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.pronounce.phoneme_emitter(, model='facebook/wav2vec2-lv-60-espeak-cv-ft', threads=None, rootdir=None)

The default [`Emitter`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Emitter): the wav2vec2 phoneme recogniser in its own env.

The env (torch, transformers) is built on first use under the data root, and the
model weights download from the Hugging Face hub then.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)], [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]]

### voxy.pronounce.phrase_readings(log_probs, vocab, readings, , before='', after='', blank=None)

Each reading’s CTC log-likelihood as the whole phrase `before + reading + after`.

The words around the flagged one are written out (IPA) and are the same in every
candidate, so the comparison isolates the word: its neighbours’ sounds cannot be
credited to a longer reading, as they are when the word is cropped or spotted alone.

```pycon
>>> vocab = ["<pad>", "ɛ", "s", "t", "l", "ə"]
>>> lp = log_probs_from_path([2, 3, 1, 4, 5], vocab_size=6)  # "(trist)e" s t ɛ l ə
>>> s = phrase_readings(lp, vocab, {"verb": "ɛ", "noun": "ɛst"}, before="st", after="lə")
>>> s["verb"] > s["noun"]
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]

### voxy.pronounce.reading_name(name)

The reading a name stands for: `"verb~liaison"` is a variant of `"verb"`.

```pycon
>>> reading_name("verb~liaison"), reading_name("noun")
('verb', 'noun')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### voxy.pronounce.render_verified(lines, checks, \*, render, emitter, words_of=<function \_transcribed_words>, max_attempts=3, padding=0.08, margin=0.5)

Render each line, and re-render the ones whose flagged words came out wrong.

A line with checks is verified ([`verify_words()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.verify_words)) after each render and
rendered again while a word is decidedly misread ([`failing()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.failing)), up to
`max_attempts` renders; a line without checks is rendered once, and a blank
line not at all (line numbers still count it, as `flag_risks` does).
[`LineTakes.chosen`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.LineTakes.chosen) is the take to keep; [`LineTakes.verified`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.LineTakes.verified) also
requires each expected reading to be confirmed (a word ASR did not find, or the
recogniser could not decide, leaves the line unverified rather than retried).

* **Parameters:**
  * **lines** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – The lines to speak, in order (line numbers start at 1).
  * **checks** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]]]) – By line number, the words to check ([`checks_by_line()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.checks_by_line)).
  * **render** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike)]) – `(text, line, attempt) -> audio path`; each call should give a
    new take (a new seed, or a service’s own variation).
    [`speech_renderer()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.speech_renderer) adapts a [`voxy.base.SpeechModel`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.SpeechModel).
  * **emitter** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)], [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]]) – The phoneme recogniser ([`phoneme_emitter()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.phoneme_emitter)).
  * **words_of** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)]]) – `audio -> timed words`; the default transcribes with
    `voxy.refprep.transcribe`.
  * **max_attempts** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Renders of one line at most.
  * **padding** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – As in [`verify_words()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.verify_words).
  * **margin** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – As in [`verify_words()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.verify_words).
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`LineTakes`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.LineTakes)]

```pycon
>>> heard = {"est": "ɛ"}  # a fake recogniser: what each word sounds like
>>> def emitter(audio, start, end):
...     vocab = ["<pad>", "ɛ", "s", "t"]
...     path = [vocab.index(s) for s in heard["est"]]
...     return log_probs_from_path(path, vocab_size=4), vocab
>>> def render(text, line, attempt):
...     heard["est"] = "ɛst" if attempt else "ɛ"  # the second take is right
...     return f"take-{line}-{attempt}.wav"
>>> words = lambda audio: [{"start": 0.0, "end": 0.3, "text": "Est"}]
>>> checks = {1: [("Est", {"verb": "ɛ", "noun": "ɛst"}, "noun")]}
>>> [result] = render_verified(["L'Est"], checks, render=render, emitter=emitter,
...                            words_of=words)
>>> [t.audio for t in result.takes], result.chosen.attempt, result.verified
(['take-1-0.wav', 'take-1-1.wav'], 1, True)
```

### voxy.pronounce.score_readings(log_probs, vocab, readings, , blank=None)

Each reading’s CTC log-likelihood per target symbol (higher is better).

Normalising by length keeps a longer reading (“ɛst”) from losing to a shorter one
(“ɛ”) just for having more symbols to pay for. `blank` defaults to the id of
[`BLANK_SYMBOL`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.BLANK_SYMBOL) in `vocab` (0 if it has none).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]

### voxy.pronounce.speech_renderer(model, voice=None, , outdir=None, take_kwarg=None, \*\*synthesize_kwargs)

A `render` for [`render_verified()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.render_verified) over a [`voxy.base.SpeechModel`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.SpeechModel).

Each take is saved as `<outdir>/<line>-<attempt>.<format>` (default outdir: a
new folder per renderer under `voxy_cache_dir("takes")`, so runs never
overwrite each other’s takes). With `take_kwarg` (e.g. `"seed"`), the attempt
number is passed to `model.synthesize` under that name, so a seeded model gives
a new take; without it, the model is simply called again.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### voxy.pronounce.spot_log_likelihood(log_probs, target, , blank=0, filler_penalty=None)

`log P` of `target` said somewhere in `log_probs`, the rest being filler.

Keyword spotting under CTC: frames before and after the target are explained by a
filler that takes each frame’s best symbol at a cost of `filler_penalty` nats.
Scoring a word inside a window that holds its neighbours, a reading wins by
matching phonemes that are really there, not by the window’s edges: a crop cut
from loose ASR word times otherwise favours the longer reading (/ɛst/ over /ɛ/).

```pycon
>>> vocab = ["<pad>", "ɛ", "s", "t", "l"]
>>> lp = log_probs_from_path([4, 1, 0, 4], vocab_size=5)  # "l ɛ l": the verb
>>> verb, noun = (spot_log_likelihood(lp, tokenize_phonemes(r, vocab)) for r in ("ɛ", "ɛst"))
>>> verb > noun
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### voxy.pronounce.spot_readings(log_probs, vocab, readings, , blank=None, filler_penalty=None)

Each reading’s [`spot_log_likelihood()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.spot_log_likelihood), less that of filler alone (higher is better).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]

### voxy.pronounce.timed_words(segments)

The timed words of ASR segments (`voxy.refprep.transcribe`’s output).

Words without times are dropped; a segment with no timed word counts as one word.

```pycon
>>> timed_words([{"words": [{"start": 0.0, "end": 0.2, "text": "a"},
...                         {"start": None, "end": None, "text": "b"}]},
...              {"start": 1.0, "end": 2.0, "text": "c", "words": []}])
[{'start': 0.0, 'end': 0.2, 'text': 'a'}, {'start': 1.0, 'end': 2.0, 'text': 'c'}]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)]

### voxy.pronounce.tokenize_phonemes(reading, vocab)

Vocabulary ids of an IPA `reading`, longest symbol first; spaces are ignored.

A reading may also be given as a sequence of symbols. Raises `ValueError` on a
symbol the recogniser does not know, since it could never be heard.

```pycon
>>> tokenize_phonemes("ɛ̃s", ["<pad>", "ɛ", "ɛ̃", "s"])
[2, 3]
```

* **Return type:**

# _autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md

# voxy.refprep

Prepare a speaker’s recordings for cloning and fine-tuning: clean, cut, transcribe, score.

```pycon
>>> from voxy import refprep
>>> clips = refprep.prepare_reference(["tape1.m4a", "tape2.mp3"], voice="ada")
>>> ref = refprep.best_references(clips)[0]
>>> ref["path"], ref["text"], ref["score"]
```

The steps, each a function you can call alone or replace:

1. `condition` (ffmpeg): any format to mono PCM WAV at `sample_rate`, with a
   high-pass, optional denoising (`denoise=`: ‘afftdn’, ‘anlmdn’, ‘deepfilternet’, or None) and
   loudness normalisation (EBU R128, `loudness_lufs`).
2. `transcribe`: timed segments and words from a local Whisper (scribed’s
   faster-whisper backend, in its own environment, see `voxy.envs`).
3. `speaker` (optional, `voxy.speakers.speaker_filter`): marks words, and
   untranscribed stretches, spoken by someone other than the target voice.
4. `plan_clips`: cut points at sentence/segment boundaries, so each clip is
   `min_seconds`-`max_seconds` long, carries its exact text, and never
   contains a marked word.
5. `score_clip`: duration, signal-to-noise estimate, clipping, level, ASR
   confidence, speaking rate and (with a speaker step) the speaker match,
   folded into a `score` in [0, 1].

`prepare_reference` runs them all and saves the clips plus `manifest.jsonl` in
the voice’s samples store (`voxy.stores.samples_store`), so any backend (a
reference clip) and fine-tuning (`voxy.finetune`, the whole set) read the same data.

### Module Attributes

| [`SPEAKER_SCORE_RANGE`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.SPEAKER_SCORE_RANGE)   | Speaker similarity mapped to the score's `speaker` part (0 at the low end, 1 at the high).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DENOISE_FILTERS`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.DENOISE_FILTERS)       | no denoising).                                                                               |
| [`DF_SAMPLE_RATE`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.DF_SAMPLE_RATE)        | DeepFilterNet works at 48 kHz; it needs an old torch/torchaudio pair, hence its own env.     |

### Functions

| [`best_references`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.best_references)(manifest, \*[, n, ...])            | The `n` best clips for zero-shot reference (length in range, best score first).         |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`close_asr`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.close_asr)()                                        | Stop the transcription workers (free their memory).                                     |

| [`conditioning_filters`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.conditioning_filters)(\*[, denoise, ...])           | The ffmpeg audio filter chain for `condition`.                                          |

### voxy.refprep.plan_clips(segments, , min_seconds=3.0, max_seconds=12.0, pad_seconds=0.12, total_seconds=None)

Clips `[{start, end, text, words}]` cut between words, ending sentences where possible.

Words accumulate until the clip passes `min_seconds` and a word ends a
sentence (or the next word would push it past `max_seconds`). Cuts fall in
the pause between two words, padded by up to `pad_seconds`. A word marked
`keep=False` (someone else’s, see `voxy.speakers`) ends the clip before it,
and the next clip starts after it.

```pycon
>>> w = lambda s, e, t: {"start": s, "end": e, "text": t, "confidence": 0.9}
>>> segs = [{"words": [w(0, 1, "One"), w(1.1, 2, "two."), w(3, 4, "Three"),
...                    w(4.1, 5, "four.")], "start": 0, "end": 5, "text": ""}]
>>> [c["text"] for c in plan_clips(segs, min_seconds=1.5, max_seconds=3)]
['One two.', 'Three four.']
>>> segs[0]["words"].insert(2, {**w(2.2, 2.6, " yes"), "keep": False})
>>> [(c["text"], c["start"]) for c in plan_clips(segs, min_seconds=1.5, max_seconds=3)]
[('One two.', 0.0), ('Three four.', 2.88)]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

  * **voice** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Voice name: clips go to `samples_store(voice)`.
  * **samples** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – A store to write to instead (`filename -> bytes`).
  * **sample_rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Conditioning (see `condition`).
  * **denoise** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Conditioning (see `condition`).
  * **loudness_lufs** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Conditioning (see `condition`).
  * **min_seconds** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Clip length bounds.

  * **language** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Force the ASR language (default: detected).
  * **transcriber** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(wav_path, language=) -> segments` (default `transcribe`).
  * **conditioner** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(src, dst, sample_rate=, filters=) -> path` (default `condition`).
  * **speaker** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(wav_path, segments) -> segments` marking other voices’ words
    (`voxy.speakers.speaker_filter`); None keeps every voice.
* **Returns:**
  one dict per clip (`key`, `path` if on disk, `text`,
  `source`, `start`, `end`, and the `score_clip` measures), best first.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.refprep.score_clip(samples, sample_rate, , words=(), text='', min_seconds=3.0, max_seconds=12.0)

Quality measures of a clip, and their combination `score` in [0, 1].

- `snr_db`: loud-frame level minus quiet-frame level (speech vs floor).
- `clipped`: fraction of samples at full scale.
- `level_db`: level of the loud frames.
- `asr_confidence`: mean Whisper word probability (low: mumbling, noise, music).
- `chars_per_second`: speaking rate (outliers: bad alignment).
- `speaker_similarity`: lowest match of a word to the target voice (words
  annotated by `voxy.speakers`; None otherwise).

```pycon
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
>>> speechy = np.concatenate([0.3 * rng.standard_normal(40000), 0.001 * rng.standard_normal(8000)])
>>> s = score_clip(speechy, 8000, text="x" * 70)
>>> s["snr_db"] > 30, 0 < s["score"] <= 1
(True, True)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### voxy.refprep.summarize(manifest)

Totals for a manifest: clips, minutes, minutes above score thresholds.

```pycon
>>> summarize([{"duration": 60, "score": 0.9}, {"duration": 30, "score": 0.4}])
{'clips': 2, 'minutes': 1.5, 'minutes_score_0.5+': 1.0, 'minutes_score_0.7+': 1.0}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### voxy.refprep.transcribe(audio, , language=None, model='large-v3-turbo', threads=None, rootdir=None)

Timed segments `[{start, end, text, confidence, words: [...]}, ...]` of `audio`.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.refprep.transcribe_text(audio, \*\*kwargs)

The transcript of `audio` as one string.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### voxy.refprep.with_deepfilternet(conditioner=None, , denoiser=None, rootdir=None)

A `conditioner` that denoises with DeepFilterNet between two ffmpeg passes.

Pass 1 converts the source to a 48 kHz mono WAV (no filters); DeepFilterNet cleans
it; pass 2 applies the usual `filters` (high-pass, loudness) and resamples to
`sample_rate`. `conditioner` (default [`condition()`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.condition)) does both ffmpeg passes.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)]

# voxy.say_model

Local speech with the macOS `say` command: free, offline, no API key, no deps.

Good for previews and drafts before spending credits on a cloud voice. Voices are
the system’s (`say -v '?'`): e.g. “Samantha”, “Daniel”, “Karen”.

```pycon
>>> SaySpeechModel(run=lambda *a, **k: None).dflt_voice
```

# _autosummary/voxy.script.html.md

# voxy.script

Render a cast script: text segments, each read by its own voice, one audio file per section.

For anything narrated by more than one voice (an audiobook with a narrator and a quoted
guide, a dialogue, a radio play). Three plain-data inputs, each a JSON-able mapping so a
person can edit them and the rest follows:

- the **script**: a list of sections `{"id", "title"?, "segments": [{"role", "text"}]}`;
- the **casting**: `{"roles": {role: voice name or None}, "takes": {section id: take},
  "default_role"?}`; a role mapped to `None` has no voice yet (its sections are listed,
  not rendered);
- the **voices**: voice name -> `{"backend"?, "init"?, "params"?, "tempo"?, "effect"?,
  "external"?}` plus how to load it (`"library": name`, `"reference": {"audio", "text"}`
  or `"voice": id-or-name` passed to the backend as is). `tempo` (pitch kept, rubberband)
  and `effect` (an ffmpeg audio filter) are finishing steps; `external` marks a voice
  synthesised elsewhere (`missing_takes` lists what it owes, `add_take` files the audio).

Files under `root`:

> segments/<key>.wav|json   one take of one segment; the key hashes (voice, settings,
> : spoken text, take number), so a take is never overwritten
>   and an edit makes a new one

> sections/<id>.mp3         a section’s takes joined: pauses, tempo, effect, loudness
> : (EBU R128) evened across voices, a gap where the voice changes

> index.json                per section: status, segments (key, role, voice), file, seconds

Render again after editing: only segments whose key changed are synthesised, and only
sections whose takes or finishing changed are rebuilt. A retake of a section is
`"takes": {"s1": 2}` in the casting (a `seed` in the voice’s params moves with the take).

```pycon
>>> script = [{"id": "s1", "segments": [{"role": "guide", "text": "Come."}, {"role": "author", "text": "I come."}]}]
>>> casting = {"roles": {"guide": "g", "author": "a"}}
>>> [(s["role"], s["voice"]) for s in plan_script(script, casting)[0]["segments"]]
[('guide', 'g'), ('author', 'a')]
```

### Functions

| [`add_take`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.add_take)(root, segment, audio, \*[, ...])       | File one take: `segments/<key>.wav` (`audio`: WAV bytes) and its `.json`.                           |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`finish_section`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.finish_section)(wavs, out, finish)               | Join takes (each `(wav path, voice spec)`) into one MP3 at `out`.                                   |
| [`lengthen_pauses`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.lengthen_pauses)(samples, sr, \*, tiers[, ...])  | `samples` (mono float array) with each inner pause lengthened by its tier's extra seconds.          |
| [`load_voice_profile`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.load_voice_profile)(spec, \*[, root])            | The voice to hand `synthesize` from a voices entry (see the module docstring).                      |
| [`missing_takes`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.missing_takes)(script, root, \*[, casting, ...]) | Segments with no take yet (by default only those of external voices), in script order.              |
| [`plan_script`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.plan_script)(script, casting, \*[, text_prep])   | Each section with its segments resolved: `{role, voice, text, tts_text, take}`.                     |
| [`render_script`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.render_script)(script, root, \*[, casting, ...]) | Render what is missing or changed, section by section in script order; return (and save) the index. |
| [`segment_key`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.segment_key)(segment, voice)                     | A take's identity: a hash of the voice (loading and settings), spoken text and take number.         |
| [`status`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.status)(root)                                    | Progress from `index.json`: counts per status, total `seconds`, `segments_by_voice`.                |

### voxy.script.add_take(root, segment, audio, , generation_seconds=None)

File one take: `segments/<key>.wav` (`audio`: WAV bytes) and its `.json`.

`segment` is an entry of `missing_takes` (or the renderer’s own), with `key` and
`voice_spec`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### voxy.script.finish_section(wavs, out, finish)

Join takes (each `(wav path, voice spec)`) into one MP3 at `out`.

Per take: pauses, then tempo, effect and loudness; a silent gap follows each take but
the last. Needs `ffmpeg` (with rubberband for `tempo`).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### voxy.script.lengthen_pauses(samples, sr, , tiers, floor_db=-35.0)

`samples` (mono float array) with each inner pause lengthened by its tier’s extra seconds.

A pause is a run of 10 ms frames `floor_db` below the loud frames (95th percentile);
it is lengthened by repeating its own middle, so the room tone carries on. Leading and
trailing silence is left as is.

```pycon
>>> tone = np.sin(np.arange(8000) / 3.0).astype(np.float32)
>>> y = np.concatenate([tone, np.zeros(4000, np.float32), tone])  # 0.5 s pause at 8 kHz
>>> len(lengthen_pauses(y, 8000, tiers=[[0.4, 0.25]])) - len(y)
2000
```

### voxy.script.load_voice_profile(spec, , root=None)

The voice to hand `synthesize` from a voices entry (see the module docstring).

### voxy.script.missing_takes(script, root, , casting=None, voices=None, text_prep=None, external_only=True)

Segments with no take yet (by default only those of external voices), in script order.

Each is `{section, role, voice, text, tts_text, take, key, voice_spec}`: hand it to
whatever renders that voice, then file the audio with `add_take(root, segment, wav)`.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.script.plan_script(script, casting, , text_prep=None)

Each section with its segments resolved: `{role, voice, text, tts_text, take}`.

`tts_text` is `text_prep(text)` (what is spoken; default: the text itself), so the
take’s key follows what the voice says, not the displayed text.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.script.render_script(script, root, \*, casting=None, voices=None, only=None, finish=None, text_prep=None, model_factory=None, voice_loader=<function load_voice_profile>, log=<built-in function print>)

Render what is missing or changed, section by section in script order; return (and save) the index.

* **Parameters:**
  * **script** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)]) – Sections `{"id", "title"?, "segments": [{"role", "text"}]}`.
  * **root** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike)) – The output folder; `casting` and `voices` default to its
    `casting.json` and `voices.json`.
  * **only** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Section ids to render (default all); the index still lists every section.
  * **finish** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Overrides of `DFLT_FINISH` (gap between voices, loudness, bitrate, pauses).
  * **text_prep** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `text -> spoken text` per segment (e.g. `voxy.speechtext` preparation).
  * **model_factory** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(backend, **init) -> SpeechModel` (default `voxy.create_speech_model`).
  * **voice_loader** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)) – `(voice spec, root=) -> voice` (default `load_voice_profile`).
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### voxy.script.segment_key(segment, voice)

A take’s identity: a hash of the voice (loading and settings), spoken text and take number.

`tempo` and `effect` are finishing steps, left out: changing them rebuilds the
section files without new takes.

```pycon
>>> a = segment_key({"tts_text": "Hi", "take": 1}, {"params": {"seed": 1}})
>>> a == segment_key({"tts_text": "Hi", "take": 1}, {"params": {"seed": 1}, "tempo": 0.8})
True
>>> a == segment_key({"tts_text": "Hi", "take": 2}, {"params": {"seed": 1}})
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### voxy.script.status(root)

Progress from `index.json`: counts per status, total `seconds`, `segments_by_voice`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)


# _autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md

# voxy.speakers

Keep one speaker: find their voice in a recording and mark everyone else’s words.

Recordings of a person are rarely just that person: an interviewer asks the
questions, someone says “yes” or “uh-huh” in the middle of an answer. A clone or a
fine-tune trained on those clips learns the other voices too. This module
compares the voice in short sliding windows with a **voice print** (the mean
ECAPA speaker embedding of the target) and marks every transcribed word, and
every untranscribed stretch of someone else’s voice, that does not match it:

```pycon
>>> from voxy import refprep, speakers
>>> print_ = speakers.voice_print("clean_answer.wav")
>>> refprep.prepare_reference(["interview.m4a"], voice="ada",
...                           speaker=speakers.speaker_filter(print_))
```

`plan_clips` then never puts a marked word, or the pause around one, inside a
clip. With no voice print, `speaker_filter()` takes each recording’s
**dominant** voice (an iterated centroid over its loud windows), which is right
for a talk or an interview where the target does most of the talking.

The embeddings come from SpeechBrain’s ECAPA-TDNN (Apache-2.0, VoxCeleb weights)
running in voxy’s isolated `speaker` environment (`SPEAKER_ENV`, built on
first use, see `voxy.envs`); everything after the embeddings is numpy, so the
logic below is testable with made-up vectors.

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_MATCH_SIMILARITY`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_MATCH_SIMILARITY)    | Cosine similarity to the voice print below which a window is someone else.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_SILENCE_MARGIN_DB`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_SILENCE_MARGIN_DB)   | neither voice.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| [`DFLT_MIN_FOREIGN_SECONDS`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_MIN_FOREIGN_SECONDS) | Untranscribed foreign stretches shorter than this are ignored (one window's wobble).                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`DFLT_FOREIGN_PAD_SECONDS`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_FOREIGN_PAD_SECONDS) | Margin added around a foreign stretch, so a cut never clips its edge into a clip.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| [`DFLT_WORD_OVERLAP`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_WORD_OVERLAP)        | A word with this share of its length inside a foreign stretch is not kept.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`DFLT_DIP_SIMILARITY`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_DIP_SIMILARITY)      | Inside a transcribed turn, a stretch is someone else's only below this (smoothed) match: one-second windows of old, noisy audio dip well below `DFLT_MATCH_SIMILARITY` on the target's own voice, so a turn that matches as a whole is only cut where the dip is deep. |
| [`DFLT_SMOOTH_WINDOWS`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_SMOOTH_WINDOWS)      | Window similarities are averaged over this many neighbours before finding stretches.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`DFLT_MIN_TURN_SECONDS`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_MIN_TURN_SECONDS)    | never kept.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

### Functions

| [`close_speaker`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.close_speaker)()                                   | Stop the embedding workers (free their memory).                                       |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`dominant_centroid`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.dominant_centroid)(vectors, \*[, iterations, ...]) | The voice heard most: re-centre on the windows most like the centroid, repeatedly.    |
| [`embed_windows`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.embed_windows)(audio, \*[, spans, window, ...])    | ECAPA embeddings of `window`-second windows every `hop` s of `audio`.                 |
| [`foreign_spans`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.foreign_spans)(windows, similarity, \*[, ...])     | Stretches where a loud window does not match the voice print, padded by `pad`.        |
| [`loud_mask`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.loud_mask)(windows, samples, sample_rate, \*)      | Windows with speech in them: loud frames within `margin_db` of the speech level.      |
| [`mark_speaker`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.mark_speaker)(segments, windows, similarity, \*)   | Annotate each timed word with `speaker_similarity` and `keep`; add gap markers.       |
| [`smooth`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.smooth)(similarity[, windows])                     | Moving average of `similarity` over `windows` neighbours (edges: the shorter mean).   |
| [`speaker_filter`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.speaker_filter)([target, threshold, ...])          | A `refprep.prepare_reference(speaker=...)` step: `(wav_path, segments) -> segments`.  |
| [`turn_similarity`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.turn_similarity)(segments, windows, ...[, loud])   | Match of each transcribed segment (a turn) to `voice_print`, from its mean window.    |
| [`voice_print`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.voice_print)(audio, \*[, spans, embed])            | The voice print of `audio` (one recording or several): the dominant voice's centroid. |

### Classes

| [`Windows`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.Windows)(times, vectors)   | Speaker embeddings of sliding windows: `times` (n, 2) seconds, unit `vectors` (n, d).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_DIP_SIMILARITY *= 0.15*

Inside a transcribed turn, a stretch is someone else’s only below this (smoothed) match:
one-second windows of old, noisy audio dip well below `DFLT_MATCH_SIMILARITY` on the
target’s own voice, so a turn that matches as a whole is only cut where the dip is deep.

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_FOREIGN_PAD_SECONDS *= 0.15*

Margin added around a foreign stretch, so a cut never clips its edge into a clip.

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_MATCH_SIMILARITY *= 0.45*

Cosine similarity to the voice print below which a window is someone else.

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_MIN_FOREIGN_SECONDS *= 0.2*

Untranscribed foreign stretches shorter than this are ignored (one window’s wobble).

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_MIN_TURN_SECONDS *= 1.0*

never kept.

* **Type:**
  Turns shorter than this are too short to attribute (”Yes.”, ”Uh-huh”)

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_SILENCE_MARGIN_DB *= 25.0*

neither voice.

* **Type:**
  Windows this far below the recording’s speech level are silence

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_SMOOTH_WINDOWS *= 3*

Window similarities are averaged over this many neighbours before finding stretches.

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_WORD_OVERLAP *= 0.25*

A word with this share of its length inside a foreign stretch is not kept.

### *class* voxy.speakers.Windows(times, vectors)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Speaker embeddings of sliding windows: `times` (n, 2) seconds, unit `vectors` (n, d).

#### similarity(voice_print)

Cosine similarity of each window to `voice_print`.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.speakers.close_speaker()

Stop the embedding workers (free their memory).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### voxy.speakers.dominant_centroid(vectors, , iterations=6, quantile=0.5)

The voice heard most: re-centre on the windows most like the centroid, repeatedly.

Clustering fragments a noisy voice into several clusters; this converges on
the majority voice instead (it needs that voice to be more than half the windows
the first mean is computed from).

```pycon
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
>>> a, b = np.eye(4)[0], np.eye(4)[1]
>>> vs = np.array([_unit(a + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(4)) for _ in range(30)]
...             + [_unit(b + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(4)) for _ in range(10)])
>>> bool(dominant_centroid(vs) @ a > 0.95)
True
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.speakers.embed_windows(audio, , spans=None, window=1.0, hop=0.1, model='speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb', threads=None, rootdir=None)

ECAPA embeddings of `window`-second windows every `hop` s of `audio`.

`spans` restricts the windows to those `(start, end)` stretches (default:
the whole file). Any sample rate; the worker resamples to 16 kHz.

* **Return type:**
  [`Windows`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.Windows)

### voxy.speakers.foreign_spans(windows, similarity, , threshold=0.45, loud=None, min_seconds=0.2, pad=0.15)

Stretches where a loud window does not match the voice print, padded by `pad`.

`threshold` is one similarity, or one per window.

Each window speaks for the `hop`-wide slot around its centre, so a short “yes”
marks about the length of the dip it causes, not a whole window.

```pycon
>>> t = np.array([[i * 0.1, i * 0.1 + 1] for i in range(20)])
>>> sim = np.array([0.8] * 8 + [0.1] * 4 + [0.8] * 8)
>>> [[round(x, 2) for x in s] for s in foreign_spans(Windows(t, None), sim, pad=0)]
[[1.25, 1.65]]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]

### voxy.speakers.loud_mask(windows, samples, sample_rate, , margin_db=25.0)

Windows with speech in them: loud frames within `margin_db` of the speech level.

```pycon
>>> w = Windows(np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), np.zeros((2, 3)))
>>> x = np.concatenate([0.3 * np.ones(8000), np.zeros(8000)])
>>> loud_mask(w, x, 8000).tolist()
[True, False]
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.speakers.mark_speaker(segments, windows, similarity, , threshold=0.45, loud=None, turns=None, dip_threshold=0.15, min_turn_seconds=1.0, word_overlap=0.25, pad=0.15, min_seconds=0.2)

Annotate each timed word with `speaker_similarity` and `keep`; add gap markers.

Without `turns`, a word is kept when the windows centred inside it match the
voice print on average. With `turns` (one match per segment, see
[`turn_similarity()`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.turn_similarity)), a word is kept when its whole segment matches and lasts
at least `min_turn_seconds`, and its `speaker_similarity` is the segment’s;
inside a segment only a deep dip (below `dip_threshold`) counts as someone else,
and a one-word sentence (“Yes.”) must match the voice print on its own.
Either way a word is dropped when `word_overlap` of it lies in a foreign
stretch. Every foreign stretch is also added as an empty word with
`keep=False` (an untranscribed “uh-huh” has no word of its own), padded by up
to `pad` and trimmed back to the kept words around it, so `refprep.plan_clips`
never puts it inside a clip. A segment without word timings is judged as one word.

```pycon
>>> t = np.array([[i * 0.1, i * 0.1 + 1] for i in range(40)])
>>> sim = np.array([0.8] * 15 + [0.1] * 5 + [0.8] * 20)
>>> w = lambda s, e, x: {"start": s, "end": e, "text": x}
>>> segs = [{"start": 0, "end": 4, "text": "a b",
...          "words": [w(0.5, 1.4, " a"), w(2.5, 3.8, " b")]}]
>>> out = mark_speaker(segs, Windows(t, None), sim)
>>> [(x["text"], x["keep"]) for x in out[0]["words"]], out[1]["words"][0]["end"]
([(' a', True), (' b', True)], 2.5)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.speakers.smooth(similarity, windows=3)

Moving average of `similarity` over `windows` neighbours (edges: the shorter mean).

```pycon
>>> smooth(np.array([1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0])).round(2).tolist()
[1.0, 0.67, 0.67, 0.67, 1.0]
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.speakers.speaker_filter(target=None, , threshold=0.45, dip_threshold=0.15, smooth_windows=3, min_turn_seconds=1.0, embed=None, \*\*embed_kwargs)

A `refprep.prepare_reference(speaker=...)` step: `(wav_path, segments) -> segments`.

Decides per transcribed segment (a turn: [`turn_similarity()`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.turn_similarity)), then cuts
deep dips inside kept turns and other voices between them ([`mark_speaker()`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.mark_speaker)).

* **Parameters:**
  * **target** (`ndarray` | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – The voice print to keep (from [`voice_print()`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.voice_print)); None takes each
    recording’s dominant voice.
  * **threshold** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Cosine similarity a turn (or a stretch between turns) needs to
    count as the target.
  * **dip_threshold** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Smoothed similarity below which a stretch inside a kept turn
    is someone else.
  * **smooth_windows** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Neighbouring windows averaged before finding stretches.
  * **min_turn_seconds** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Shorter turns are never kept.
  * **embed** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Windows`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.Windows)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(path, **embed_kwargs) -> Windows` (default [`embed_windows()`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.embed_windows)).
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]]

### voxy.speakers.turn_similarity(segments, windows, voice_print, , loud=None)

Match of each transcribed segment (a turn) to `voice_print`, from its mean window.

Averaging the embeddings over a whole turn is far steadier than any one window
on noisy audio: it is what tells an interviewer’s question from an answer. None
for a segment with no (loud) window centred in it.

```pycon
>>> t = np.array([[i * 0.1, i * 0.1 + 1] for i in range(40)])
>>> v = np.array([np.eye(2)[0]] * 20 + [np.eye(2)[1]] * 20)
>>> turn_similarity([{"start": 0, "end": 2}, {"start": 2.6, "end": 4.4}],
...                 Windows(t, v), np.eye(2)[0])
[1.0, 0.0]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]

### voxy.speakers.voice_print(audio, , spans=None, embed=None, \*\*embed_kwargs)

The voice print of `audio` (one recording or several): the dominant voice’s centroid.

Pass recordings (or `spans` of one) where the target speaks alone, and this is
simply their voice; over mixed recordings it is whoever speaks most.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`


# _autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md

# voxy.speechtext

Display text vs speech text, and spotting words a model may misread.

A text a person reads and the text a model should be given are not always the same.
Measured case (French, a Qwen3-TTS clone): a verse line starting with a capitalised
verb, “Est parti” after a line “Mon frere”, was read as the noun /est/ (“l’Est”) in 4
of 4 takes; lowercased (“est parti”) it was read correctly in 4 of 4. The capital, not
the line break, is the trigger: line-initial “Est” tokenises like the noun in “l’Est”.
ASR checks cannot catch this (Whisper hears “est” either way), so the fix is upstream:

1. [`prepare_speech_text()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.prepare_speech_text) turns display text into speech text: it lowercases a
   *verse-initial* capital that does not start a sentence (keeping deliberate capitals:
   words also capitalised mid-line, or named in `keep`), then applies a per-language
   respelling table and proper-name aliases, and returns every change it made.
2. [`flag_risks()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.flag_risks) lists the words of a text a model may misread (heteronyms you
   supply, e.g. from Lexique; more detectors plug in through `extra`), saying which
   ones sit where the capital trigger bites. [`pos_detector()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.pos_detector) is one such
   detector: it tags the text and, for heteronyms whose part of speech picks the
   reading (French “est”: verb /ɛ/, noun /ɛst/), names the `expected` reading;
   [`llm_detector()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.llm_detector) asks a language model for the risky words and their readings.

Engines differ in what they accept: for several local models text is the only lever
(they take no phonemes or SSML), so this is a text-level step; it plugs into
`LocalCloneSpeechModel(text_prep=...)`. Verifying the audio itself (phoneme
recognition of the flagged words) is [`voxy.pronounce`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#module-voxy.pronounce).

```pycon
>>> text = "Mon frere\nEst parti\nLoin d'ici."
>>> prepare_speech_text(text).speech
"Mon frere\nest parti\nloin d'ici."
>>> prepare_speech_text(text, keep={"Est", "Loin"}).speech == text
True
```

### voxy.speechtext.llm_detector(, chat=None, language='French', prompt='You help a text-to-speech system avoid misreadings. Below is a $language text, its lines numbered. List the words a speech model may misread: heteronyms (words with more than one pronunciation, such as French "est" as a verb or as a noun), names, abbreviations. For each, give the line, the word exactly as written, short names of its possible readings, and the reading this context needs.\\n\\nAnswer with a JSON list only, one object per word:\\n[{"line": 2, "word": "est", "readings": ["verb", "noun"], "expected": "verb", "why": "..."}]\\nUse "expected": null when the context does not decide. Answer [] if nothing is risky.\\n\\n$text\\n')

A [`flag_risks()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.flag_risks) `extra` detector that asks a language model for risky words.

The model’s proposals are kept only when the word is really on the line it names,
and an `expected` reading only when it is one of the proposed `readings`; a
reply that is not a JSON list proposes nothing.

* **Parameters:**
  * **chat** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `prompt -> reply text`; default `aix.chat` (`pip install 'voxy[aix]'`,
    keys and model from aix’s own config). Each call costs a model request.
  * **language** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The text’s language, named in the prompt.
  * **prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – A `string.Template` with `$language` and `$text` (numbered lines).
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Risk`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.Risk)]]

```pycon
>>> fake = lambda prompt: '[{"line": 1, "word": "est", "readings": ["verb", "noun"], "expected": "verb"}]'
>>> [(r.line, r.word, r.expected) for r in llm_detector(chat=fake)("Il est parti")]
[(1, 'est', 'verb')]
```

### voxy.speechtext.prepare_speech_text(text, , lowercase_verse_initial=True, keep=(), respellings=None, aliases=None, transforms=())

Display text in, speech text out, with a record of every change.

* **Parameters:**
  * **text** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The text as a reader sees it (lines may be verse lines).
  * **lowercase_verse_initial** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Lowercase a line-initial capital that does not start
    a sentence (the first line of a paragraph, or a line after one ending in
    `. ! ? …`, keeps its capital).
  * **keep** ([`Collection`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Collection)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Words whose capital is deliberate and stays (compared exactly). Words
    also capitalised elsewhere in a line are kept automatically.
  * **respellings** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Word -> same-sound spelling, whole words, case-insensitive (e.g.
    a language’s ambiguous forms written unambiguously).
  * **aliases** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Proper name -> pronounceable spelling, whole words, case-insensitive.
  * **transforms** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – Extra `text -> text` steps applied last, over the whole text.
* **Return type:**
  [`SpeechText`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.SpeechText)
* **Returns:**
  A [`SpeechText`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.SpeechText).

# _autosummary/voxy.stores.html.md

# voxy.stores

Where voxy keeps its data: voice records and audio, as `MutableMapping` stores.

Layout under the data root (`$VOXY_DATA_DIR`, default `~/.local/share/voxy`
via `config2py`), one subfolder per kind of data:

> voices/{name}.json        voice records: aliases, consent, one profile per backend
> samples/{name}/{file}     prepared audio a clone is made from
> sources/{name}/{file}     raw source media the samples were cut from

Callers take a store as an argument (`voices=`, `samples=`) and never build
paths themselves, so moving the data elsewhere (another folder, S3, a database)
means passing a different `MutableMapping`. Folders are created on first write.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
>>> voices = voices_store(rootdir=root)
>>> voices["ada"] = {"name": "ada"}
>>> list(voices), voices["ada"]
(['ada'], {'name': 'ada'})
>>> samples = samples_store("ada", rootdir=root)
>>> samples["clip.wav"] = b"RIFF"
>>> list(samples)
['clip.wav']
```

### Functions

| [`audio_store`](_autosummary/voxy.stores.html.md#voxy.stores.audio_store)(kind, voice, \*[, rootdir])   | Audio files of one voice and kind, `filename -> bytes`.                       |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`check_voice_name`](_autosummary/voxy.stores.html.md#voxy.stores.check_voice_name)(name)                    | Return `name` if it can name a voice (one path segment), else raise.          |
| [`kind_dir`](_autosummary/voxy.stores.html.md#voxy.stores.kind_dir)(kind, \*parts[, rootdir])        | The folder for one kind of data, optionally a subfolder (not created here).   |
| [`samples_store`](_autosummary/voxy.stores.html.md#voxy.stores.samples_store)(voice, \*[, rootdir])       | The prepared samples a clone of `voice` is made from.                         |
| [`sources_store`](_autosummary/voxy.stores.html.md#voxy.stores.sources_store)(voice, \*[, rootdir])       | The raw source media `voice`'s samples were cut from.                         |
| [`voices_store`](_autosummary/voxy.stores.html.md#voxy.stores.voices_store)(\*[, rootdir])               | Voice records, `name -> dict`, as `voices/{name}.json` (other files ignored). |
| [`voxy_data_dir`](_autosummary/voxy.stores.html.md#voxy.stores.voxy_data_dir)()                           | The data root: `$VOXY_DATA_DIR` if set, else the platform's app-data folder.  |

### voxy.stores.check_voice_name(name)

Return `name` if it can name a voice (one path segment), else raise.

```pycon
>>> check_voice_name("ada")
'ada'
>>> check_voice_name("../x")
```

# _autosummary/voxy.textsplit.html.md

# voxy.textsplit

Split long text (a chapter) into chunks a speech model can say in one breath.

Local cloning models drift, rush or hallucinate past roughly 20-40 seconds of
speech, so long text is spoken chunk by chunk and the audio joined with
controlled pauses. Paragraphs are kept apart (they get a longer pause); inside a
paragraph, whole sentences are packed into chunks of at most `max_chars`, and
only a sentence longer than that is cut, at a clause break if it has one.

```pycon
>>> split_text("One. Two!\n\nThree is a longer sentence, with a clause.", max_chars=20)
[['One. Two!'], ['Three is a longer', 'sentence,', 'with a clause.']]
```

### Module Attributes

| [`ABBREVIATIONS`](_autosummary/voxy.textsplit.html.md#voxy.textsplit.ABBREVIATIONS)   | Words ending in a period that don't end a sentence ("Mr.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|

| [`split_sentences`](_autosummary/voxy.textsplit.html.md#voxy.textsplit.split_sentences)(paragraph)        | The sentences of `paragraph` (whitespace normalised).                        |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`split_text`](_autosummary/voxy.textsplit.html.md#voxy.textsplit.split_text)(text, \*[, max_chars]) | Paragraphs of chunks: `[[chunk, ...], ...]`, each chunk at most `max_chars`. |

# _autosummary/voxy.voicestudio_model.html.md

# voxy.voicestudio_model

Local description-prompted speech through VoiceStudio (Parler-TTS and friends).

A voice here is a *text description* (“a warm, low female voice, close to the
microphone”), not a recording: `voice` may be that string or a `VoiceProfile`
made by `design_voice`. Nothing is uploaded; weights run locally (CPU works,
slowly) and are fetched from Hugging Face on first use (`model_id=`; the default
is several GB, so `pip install 'voxy[voicestudio]'` does not download them).

The model call is a seam: `generate(text, description) -> (waveform, sample_rate)`
is injectable, so tests (and other VoiceStudio architectures) never load weights.

```pycon
>>> model = VoiceStudioSpeechModel(generate=lambda text, description: ([0.0] * 8, 8000))
>>> model.synthesize("Hi", "a calm voice").format
'wav'
```

### Classes

|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|

# _autosummary/voxy.wavutil.html.md

# voxy.wavutil

Mono PCM WAV in and out as float arrays, plus the few edits narration needs.

Every local backend and the reference-prep step exchange 16-bit PCM WAV files;
this module turns them into `float32` arrays in `[-1, 1]` and back, trims
silence, and joins pieces with pauses, using only numpy and the standard library.

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> data = write_wav(np.array([0.0, 0.5, -0.5], dtype=np.float32), 8000)
>>> samples, sr = read_wav(data)
>>> sr, np.round(samples, 3).tolist()
(8000, [0.0, 0.5, -0.5])
```

### Functions

| [`frame_db`](_autosummary/voxy.wavutil.html.md#voxy.wavutil.frame_db)(samples, sample_rate, \*[, frame_ms])   | RMS level (dBFS) of consecutive `frame_ms` frames.                                |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`read_wav`](_autosummary/voxy.wavutil.html.md#voxy.wavutil.read_wav)(source)                                 | `(samples, sample_rate)` of a PCM WAV (path or bytes), channels averaged.         |
| [`resample`](_autosummary/voxy.wavutil.html.md#voxy.wavutil.resample)(samples, from_rate, to_rate)            | Linear-interpolation resampling (enough to join pieces; use ffmpeg for masters).  |
| [`silence`](_autosummary/voxy.wavutil.html.md#voxy.wavutil.silence)(ms, sample_rate)                         | `ms` milliseconds of silence.                                                     |
| [`trim_silence`](_autosummary/voxy.wavutil.html.md#voxy.wavutil.trim_silence)(samples, sample_rate, \*[, ...])    | Drop leading and trailing frames quieter than `threshold_db` (keeping `keep_ms`). |
| [`write_wav`](_autosummary/voxy.wavutil.html.md#voxy.wavutil.write_wav)(samples, sample_rate)                  | Mono 16-bit PCM WAV bytes from floats in `[-1, 1]` (clipped).                     |
